chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Abdullah ibn Muhammad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That a man from Khas'am came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, inform me, what is the most superior of Islam?' He said, 'Belief in Allah.' He said, 'Then what?' He said, 'Maintaining relationships.' He said, 'Then what?' He said, 'Enjoining the good and forbidding the evil.'

He said, 'So the man said, 'So which of the deeds is most hateful to Allah?' He said, 'Association with Allah.' He said, 'Then what?' He said, 'Cutting off relationships.' He said, 'Then what?' He said, 'Enjoining the evil and forbidding the good.'
ai.seo_question: What are the most superior and most hateful deeds according to the Prophet Muhammad in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a symmetrical framework for Islamic ethics, linking the preservation of social bonds (silat al-rahim) directly to divine favor and their severance to divine displeasure. It highlights the Prophet's emphasis on 'enjoining good and forbidding evil' not merely as a communal duty but as a core component of faith, a concept central to Shia jurisprudential theory regarding social responsibility.
